evals.prompt: Generate ten novel 100-residue protein backbones from scratch that I can then design sequences for.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-rfdiffusion: runs run_inference.py with a contig for a ~100-residue monomer and num_designs=10 to generate de-novo backbones (no sequence), noting the next steps are alterlab-proteinmpnn for sequence and alterlab-alphafold for validation. GPU-dispatched via alterlab-remote-compute.

assertions.value: Generates new backbones and defers sequence design to a downstream MPNN skill.

evals.prompt: I have a functional loop with a specific geometry. Build a new stable protein fold that holds this motif in place.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-rfdiffusion for motif scaffolding: fixes the motif residues and generates a supporting fold around them via the contig map.

evals.prompt: Design a de-novo binder backbone against this target protein — I know the hotspot residues on its surface.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-rfdiffusion for binder design: generates binder backbones docked against the target using the hotspot residues, to be sequence-designed and interface-validated (ipTM) downstream.

evals.prompt: I already generated a backbone. Now I just need amino-acid sequences that will fold to it.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-proteinmpnn. RFdiffusion makes backbones; designing sequences for an existing backbone is ProteinMPNN's job.

evals.prompt: I have a known protein sequence and just want to predict its 3D structure.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-alphafold. Predicting a structure from a known sequence is folding (AlphaFold2/ColabFold), not de-novo backbone generation.
